question: When carrying passengers or cargo on a motorcycle, which of the following regulations is correct?
options: (1) Small light motorcycles, heavy motorcycles, and regular light motorcycles may carry one passenger if there is a fixed seat behind the rider.
(2) For cargo loading: small light motorcycles must not exceed 30 kg; regular light motorcycles must not exceed 60 kg; heavy motorcycles must not exceed 90 kg.

• Helmets: Must wear an approved CNS-certified safety helmet firmly fastened by the chin strap (NT$500 fine for unfastened/missing helmet).
• Pillion Passenger: Must sit astride the rear seat facing forward (maximum 1 passenger on heavy motorcycles; 0 on light mopeds).
• Children on Footrest: Strictly PROHIBITED to place children or babies standing/sitting in the front footrest pedal area.

❌ Why Other Options are Wrong:
• Option (1) (Small light motorcycles, heavy motorcycles, and regular light motorcycles may carry one passenger if there is a fixed seat behind the rider.): Placing passengers on footboards obstructs handlebars and causes severe ejection injuries during hard braking.
• Option (2) (For cargo loading: small light motorcycles must not exceed 30 kg; regular light motorcycles must not exceed 60 kg; heavy motorcycles must not exceed 90 kg.): Unfastened helmets easily fly off upon impact before the head strikes the pavement.

💡 Pro Study Tip: Helmet must be CNS approved + firmly buckled; Pillion passenger must sit astride rear seat facing forward!

question: If an intersection does not have a left-turn waiting area, and a motorcycle traveling in the left-turn lane crosses the stop line and stops inside the intersection for a left turn when the straight green arrow is on, how is this behavior classified?
options: (1) Legally entering the intersection under the straight arrow signal and stopping; no violation.
(2) Violates the rule of not following markings and signals when turning.
(3) Considered running a red light and should be cited under Article 53 of the Road Traffic Management and Penalty Act.
explanation:
🎯 Why Choice (2) is Correct: In Taiwan, small motorcycles (<250cc) must perform a Two-Stage Left Turn (Hook Turn / 兩段式左轉) when: 1) A two-stage left turn sign is posted, OR 2) On multi-lane roads with 3 or more lanes, OR 3) Where the inner lane is marked 'No Motorcycles' (禁行機車). Direct left turns from the outer lane cross oncoming traffic and create deadly collision hazards.

❌ Why Other Options are Wrong:
• Option (1) (Legally entering the intersection under the straight arrow signal and stopping; no violation.): Cutting across active lanes into the inner lane exposes the rider to high-speed rear-end and t-bone collisions.
• Option (3) (Considered running a red light and should be cited under Article 53 of the Road Traffic Management and Penalty Act.): Violates mandatory traffic intersection routing laws in Taiwan.

💡 Pro Study Tip: 3+ lanes or 'No Motorcycle' inner lane = Mandatory Two-Stage Hook Turn into the waiting box!

question: When a motorcycle makes a two-stage left turn at an intersection with a designated waiting area, which of the following statements about entering the waiting area is correct?

(2) Use the right- turn lane to enter the waiting area to avoid obstructing straight-going traffic.

🎯 Why Choice (1) is Correct: In Taiwan, small motorcycles (<250cc) must perform a Two-Stage Left Turn (Hook Turn / 兩段式左轉) when: 1) A two-stage left turn sign is posted, OR 2) On multi-lane roads with 3 or more lanes, OR 3) Where the inner lane is marked 'No Motorcycles' (禁行機車). Direct left turns from the outer lane cross oncoming traffic and create deadly collision hazards.

❌ Why Other Options are Wrong:
• Option (2) (Use the right- turn lane to enter the waiting area to avoid obstructing straight-going traffic.): Cutting across active lanes into the inner lane exposes the rider to high-speed rear-end and t-bone collisions.

💡 Pro Study Tip: 3+ lanes or 'No Motorcycle' inner lane = Mandatory Two-Stage Hook Turn into the waiting box!
